- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid overcorrecting downward; add 2–5% buffer to prevent premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 5-day average is trending down and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, apply mild mean reversion bias toward prior 10-day average.  
- If forecast spikes >10% above recent 18-day high, flag for correction — especially if sentiment is positive but recent sentiment has been volatile or mixed.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.6 → -0.3 → +0.7), reduce forecast volatility and favor smoother, lagged trend alignment.  
- For forecasts with high error variance (MAE > 2.5), prioritize sentiment-weighted smoothing over raw trend extrapolation.
